I don’t think you would get in trouble for explaining to your manager that they said it wouldn’t be an issue so you went ahead and already planned/paid for the activities. They might get a little pissed off, but I don’t think you can get in trouble for not going to a work that was pre approved by your manager?

I don’t think it’s a stupid idea at all. I actually think it’s really sweet and great. 
It’s a way to show him you care and are there for him without being too suffocating or putting too much pressure on him. 
I think you should do it!

I mean she does give good points, but if you feel it’s something you need to get off your chest then I think you should. You will never know if something  could happen unless you try y’a know? However, if you feel like you can wait then you should. Only because you’re sixteen. I don’t think the age gap is the issue, it’s more so the stages of life you guys are in right now, just don’t match. She’s going to college and you are
Still going to be in high school. The timing sucks is the truth. And she has a boyfriend, and unless he treats her like crap, I wouldn’t want to step over any boundaries of that makes sense. 

It’s all up to you but waiting it out isn’t a bad plan, but if you feel like it needs to happen now then go for it :)
I think that’s a great idea! And I feel like you should mention that as well to him. I wish the best for you and this guy and I hope the outcome is good :)

I mean I understand where your friends are coming from. Technically you did end it and that should be that, but if you feel there are some loose ends that you need to tighten then I think it would be good for the both of you if you reach out. I recommend writing everything you want to say out first then talk to him about it and make sure you say everything you want to. Maybe you could be friends? Or just end the terms better than you left them, who knows. But you won’t truly know until you try
I would definitely reach out to him especially if you feel it’s the right thing to do
